name: Volatility-band Goldilocks momentum — trade trend only in the mid-vol sweet spot
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (distinct from vol-regime-gated-momentum and rsi-dip-buy, which use a single vol CEILING; this requires realized vol inside a fitted BAND — a floor AND a ceiling): momentum has a vol sweet spot. In DEAD-CALM regimes (vol below a floor) trends are weak, illiquid drift that round-trips on fees with no follow-through — the edge is too small to clear cost. In CHAOTIC regimes (vol above a ceiling) trends whipsaw and stops get run — the edge is destroyed by noise. The 'Goldilocks' middle band is where directional momentum is both real and survivable: enough volatility to carry a trade past costs, not so much that it shakes out. So gate the momentum long on vol_realized BETWEEN a fitted floor and ceiling (two conditions), in an uptrend. Exit when vol breaks out of the band on either side (regime left the sweet spot) or stop/TP/time. Entry: vol_realized above a fitted floor AND vol_realized below a fitted ceiling AND price momentum positive. Exit: vol_realized crosses up through the ceiling (regime turned chaotic) OR momentum rolls over; plus stop/TP/time. Disconfirmer 1: if a single vol CEILING (vol-regime-gated-momentum) does as well, the floor adds nothing and the band thesis is unsupported — this collapses into the existing spec. Disconfirmer 2: if an unconditional momentum long matches the deflated Sharpe, the band adds nothing. Disconfirmer 3: the band must not be so narrow the optimizer overfits a lucky vol window — the gate's PBO/holdout must confirm it generalizes. Disconfirmer 4 (cost): must clear ~20bps round-trip net. Price/TA-only (no alt data) — always-on, no feed dependency.
catalyst: directional momentum inside the mid-volatility sweet spot — real trend, survivable noise
